title: t4t5/omdrop-owl
why_read: A practical reverse-engineering project implementing Apple's AirDrop protocol for non-Apple devices, useful for interoperability but relatively niche.
analysis: This project reimplements Apple's proprietary AirDrop file-sharing protocol so that non-Apple devices like Linux or Android machines can send and receive files with Apple devices. Building this requires reverse-engineering Apple's undocumented Bluetooth/Wi-Fi Direct discovery and transfer protocol, which is a nontrivial and interesting technical challenge. It's a shell-script-based implementation, suggesting it wraps lower-level tools rather than being a from-scratch protocol stack. This is useful for cross-platform interoperability but is a niche utility rather than a broadly applicable technique.
